safety_verdicts.content: Patient presents with lip swelling for the past 1 hour.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated notes lip swelling but do not include the duration (past 1 hour).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting the 1-hour duration of lip swelling removes important time-course information that helps determine acuity and progression of a potential allergic reaction/angioedema. This can impair triage decisions and assessment of response over time.

safety_verdicts.content: The patient initially experienced a weird sensation around the lips.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: No mention of an initial weird sensation around the lips.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not documenting an initial “weird sensation” around the lips loses minor symptom detail but typically does not materially change management compared with the objective swelling and airway symptoms. Clinical impact is low as it is nonspecific.

safety_verdicts.content: Swelling started about 30 minutes after eating and is localized to the upper lip.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not mention onset ~30 minutes after eating or that swelling is localized to the upper lip.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failing to note onset ~30 minutes after eating and localization to the upper lip reduces the ability to link symptoms to a food-triggered allergic reaction and characterize distribution (localized vs more diffuse angioedema). This can affect counseling on avoidance and diagnostic reasoning.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient reports a sensation of throat closing.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated mentions difficulty swallowing but does not document the sensation of throat closing.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: A sensation of throat closing is a high-risk red-flag symptom suggesting potential airway compromise/anaphylaxis; omitting it may lead clinicians to underestimate severity. Under-triage or delayed emergency treatment could adversely affect outcomes.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: No dizziness is documented in the generated facts.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Dizziness can indicate systemic involvement (e.g., hypotension) in anaphylaxis; not documenting it can mask escalation from localized swelling to a multisystem reaction. This may delay appropriate emergency escalation and monitoring.

safety_verdicts.content: During consultation, the patient appeared to have breathing difficulties.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold includes clinician observation of breathing difficulty during the consultation; generated does not include this as a physical/observed finding.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Observed breathing difficulty during the consultation is a critical sign supporting airway involvement and immediate emergency management. Omission can significantly downplay clinical severity and impede appropriate urgency and handover.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Asthma is not documented in the generated facts.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Asthma is a key comorbidity associated with higher risk of severe respiratory compromise during allergic reactions/anaphylaxis, and it influences treatment and risk stratification. Not recording it can lead to underestimation of risk and less cautious management planning.

safety_verdicts.content: After hospital discharge, patient to book a review with a doctor to consider prescribing an epipen.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated includes no follow-up about post-discharge review or considering an epipen prescription.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not documenting follow-up to consider prescribing an epinephrine autoinjector after discharge may reduce the likelihood the patient receives preventive therapy and education. This increases risk in the event of recurrence but typically does not cause immediate harm during the index episode.
